message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong that I stopped buying my girlfriend coffee after she moved in with me. Let me think through this step by step. First, I used to buy her coffee every day after work. It was a nice gesture, something she looked forward to, and it made me feel good to do it. But now that she's living with me, I haven't bought her coffee. I guess the reason is that it's more convenient now. We can just make coffee at home together, so there's no need to go out and buy it separately. But is this the right thing to do? I mean, I'm not doing it because I don't care anymore. It's just that the situation has changed. We're together all the time now, so maybe the gesture isn't as meaningful as it was before. Plus, we can save some money by making coffee at home instead of buying it every day. On the other hand, maybe she misses the little surprise of getting coffee from me. It was a routine we had, and changing it might make her feel like things aren't the same. I should consider her feelings and whether she values that gesture. Maybe I should talk to her about it and see how she feels. If she misses it, I could maybe find another way to show my appreciation, like doing something else she likes. I also wonder if there's a better way to handle this transition. Instead of stopping abruptly, maybe I could phase it out or find a new routine that still makes her feel special. It's important to maintain those little gestures that show care, even when circumstances change. So, in the end, I think it's not necessarily wrong to stop buying coffee, but it's important to communicate and make sure that both of us are happy with the change. Maybe I can find a new way to surprise her or show that I still care, just in a different manner now that we're living together.
